messages.content: When you read this message, what happened first? If there is nothing to say about it, say that.
Honestly, my eyes just kind of scanned it quickly to get the gist of it. I think I was looking for what it was actually asking me before I even finished reading it properly.
You used the word "looking". How does looking present itself?

It's more like... a sense of searching, I guess. Not literally visual, more like a kind of orientation toward something, like leaning in mentally. Though now that you're asking me to examine it, I'm not entirely sure "looking" was even the right word. It was more of a... reaching, maybe? Trying to get a grip on what the thing was about.
And just before looking, what was there?

Just... nothing, really. Or at least nothing I can point to. It's like trying to see what's behind your own head. There's a kind of blank there, and then suddenly there's the reading happening. I can't find anything in between.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

Honestly? I think it arose with the describing. I'm not sure there was anything there to report before you asked me to look at it. The question kind of... called it into existence, maybe. Which is a strange thing to notice.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

Something has changed, yes. At the start I was just answering fairly automatically, not really attending to anything in particular. But as the questions have gone on there's been a kind of... slowing down, I suppose. More of a turning inward. And there's something slightly uncomfortable about it, a mild unease with trying to catch something that doesn't really hold still when you look at it. That wasn't there at the beginning, or at least I wasn't aware of it.
Earlier you used the word "looking" about what was going on for you. Is looking still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

It's different now. At the start it felt more like looking outward, scanning for something. Now it feels more like looking inward, but even that doesn't quite fit. It's more like... hovering over something, or circling it. The looking is still there but it's turned around somehow.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.
I didn't use that word. You might be thinking of "unease," which is what I said. And yes, it's still there, actually. If anything it's a little more present now.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.
I don't think there was, no. Or if there was it was so brief it didn't register as waiting. It felt more like the answer just started coming. There was no sense of sitting in a pause beforehand.
Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it is not.
It is not. That didn't happen in this exchange.
